description:
Problem
ZAQ download_document accepts optional document_mime_type and forwards it to materialization. CommunicationMedia declares materialization_options/0 as [], so valid WhatsApp attachment handles fail with :invalid_materialization_options before provider dispatch.

Evidence
Read-only IEx investigation of transcript ff01b6b0-b584-41e0-8bed-92efcdf973a0 in zaq_feat_whatsapp_integration, 2026-10-15:
- Positions 6, 19, 36 (10:17, 11:19, 11:55 UTC): download_document called with materialization_handle and document_mime_type=image/jpeg; all returned invalid_materialization_options.
- Position 10 (10:18 UTC): exact same handle, without MIME option, succeeded and image was described.
- All four handle strings were identical. The assistant's later claim of an invalid/expired handle did not match the tool error.
- IEx reproduction: Zaq.Materialization.materialize_with_handler(Zaq.Channels.Materializers.CommunicationMedia, %{}, %{}, %{"document_mime_type" => "image/jpeg"}) returns {:error, :invalid_materialization_options}.

Ownership and locations
ZAQ owns this mismatch; rejection occurs before jido_chat_whatsapp is invoked.
- lib/zaq/agent/tools/data_source/download_document.ex: schema and materialization_options/1
- lib/zaq/materialization.ex: materialize_with_handler/4 and validate_options/2
- lib/zaq/channels/materializers/communication_media.ex: materialization_options/0

Action reuse assessment
Operation: download_document / communication-media materialization.
Candidates: existing DownloadDocument Action, Zaq.Materialization, CommunicationMedia handler.
Decision: extend/align the existing contract; no new Action or parallel download path.
Boundary: preserve handle verification, source authorization, connector routing, and NodeRouter dispatch.
Contract: supported tool inputs must be compatible with the selected materializer; document export behavior must remain intact.
Verification: focused Action-to-materializer regression tests and existing domain tests.

Acceptance criteria
1. A valid communication-image handle with the advertised source MIME option does not fail due to this contract mismatch; establish the intended handler-specific option policy.
2. Handle-only materialization remains successful.
3. Data-source source/export MIME behavior is preserved.
4. Unsupported options and authorization checks remain enforced according to the explicit contract.
5. Regression coverage exercises the actual DownloadDocument-to-materializer path.
6. Follow repository validation lifecycle; obtain human approval before changing existing test behavior.

Scope
Fix the MIME contract mismatch only. Quoted-image attachment resolution and general agent error interpretation are separate follow-ups. No implementation was performed during diagnosis.

Signed locator MIME remains authoritative; no export support or weakened unknown-option validation. Reuse DownloadDocument Action -> Materialization -> existing Channels dispatch. Backend regression; no new browser E2E needed.

User requested discarding this implementation to restart from a clean baseline. All associated uncommitted code, documentation and test changes were removed. Working tree is clean at 4281f333c. User requested a failing regression test on the clean baseline. Test first proves handle-only success, then expects the identical download to succeed with the advertised matching source MIME. No production changes or existing-test behavior changes. Concrete incident regression; no browser E2E or broad property generator needed.

Added test/zaq/agent/tools/data_source/download_document_mime_regression_test.exs only. Confirmed red: 1 test, 1 failure at the matching-MIME Jido.Exec call, returning Jido.Action.Error.ExecutionFailureError with Record materialization failed: :invalid_materialization_options. The preceding handle-only call and provider-dispatch assertion pass with the exact same signed handle and authorized actor. mix q passes. No production code or existing tests changed. Intentionally left failing as requested; no full precommit because the requested artifact is a red regression.

Follow-up zaq-pcj tracks the clean-baseline shared tool-contract fix. User requires download_document_mime_regression_test.exs to remain byte-for-byte untouched and pass; its SHA-256 is recorded in zaq-pcj. Previous implementation remains discarded.
